newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Serbs duck arms with WW2 tanks - OSCE.
newsitem.headline: Serbs duck arms with WW2 tanks - OSCE.

text.p: Bosnian Serbs are exploiting an exclusion clause in a regional arms control pact to keep a number of World War Two tanks, insisting they are destined for export, a western official said on Wednesday.
Bosnian Serbs are signitaries to the sub-regional arms control pact agreed in Florence on June 16, along with the Moslem-Croat federation, Croatia and Yugoslavia.
The agreement limits weapons each signatory can have, but also provides exceptions for weapons in manufacture, research, museums, arms awaiting disposal and arms destined for export.

"Exceptions are meant to be exceptions. I cannot give you exact numbers (of weapons)...but it is a significant number and it is a very significant problem," a spokesman for the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) said.
The agreement provides for gradual reductions in numbers of tanks, artillery, combat vehicles, aircraft and helicopters.

The United States said on Tuesday that the Bosnian Serbs had "exempted hundreds of pieces of equipment through abuse of the counting rules and they have declared a reduction liability that, in fact, entails very few reductions on their part."
The Serbs have apparently avoided their limit by claiming the tanks were designated for export.
The OSCE spokesman said that a pattern should be established to determine how many tanks the Serbs exported in previous years in order to determine how many they could keep for export.
"Most of the tanks that have been put in this category are old T-34 (and) T-55 tanks that are, let's say, difficult to (sell)... on the international arms market," he said.
Soviet-made T-34 tanks are World War Two relics and T-55s slightly "younger" by several years.
An OSCE official who asked not to be named said he believed the number of tanks Serbs were trying to keep was less than 200.
The spokesman said although there were problems in under-reporting he did not want to create an impression that there were hidden weapons in Bosnia.
